page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 64-bit ARM AWS Graviton processors. The system delivers 96 physical cores running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, eliminating hardware multithreading overhead. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per physical core.

Network connectivity operates with a 200 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The platform provides direct hardware access without virtualization overhead or hypervisor abstractions. There are no onboard local storage drives and no dedicated graphics accelerators present in the hardware bundle, requiring reliance on external networked storage volumes for persistent data operations.

From an architectural standpoint, this bare-metal configuration offers high compute density across 96 dedicated ARM cores without resource contention. The balanced memory footprint and high networking capacity support large-scale containerization clusters, distributed application runtimes, continuous integration pipelines, and memory-balanced microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores powered by AWS arm64 Graviton processors clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server provides a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with 384.0 GB of RAM, or 4.0 GB per core, with single-threaded physical execution cores and no hypervisor layer. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data transfer across distributed environments. The configuration includes no onboard local storage and no hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage solutions for stateful workloads. Because of its dense arm64 core count, direct hardware control, and high networking throughput, the m8gb.metal-24xl is suited for large-scale container orchestration, high-throughput microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed enterprise application platforms.
